conditions.name: Decision Flow
conditions.summary: Decision Flow is limiting organizational performance. Decisions appear to depend on centralized authority, approval loops, or unclear governance rather than distributed operating judgment. The strongest drivers are Governancefriction, Decisionlatency, Authority Centralized, Centralized Governance Bottleneck, and Strategic Alignment Drift Is Weakening Execution. If ignored, throughput slows because unresolved decisions accumulate around a small number of leaders or approval points. This deserves executive attention because it has broad organizational leverage. If improved, the organization should move faster as teams gain clearer authority to resolve routine ambiguity without escalation. This is a new condition-level signal. Discovery has not yet observed enough history to distinguish whether Decision Flow is persistent, temporary, or recently changed. Decision Flow appears connected to Leadership Dependency, Operating Model, and Strategic Alignment upstream and may influence Coordination System and Execution Capacity downstream.
conditions.whyItMatters: Decision flow determines how quickly the organization can resolve ambiguity and move work forward. Decision Flow is constrained because the evidence suggests decisions appear to depend on centralized authority, approval loops, or unclear governance rather than distributed operating judgment.
